title: Designed 404 in the site's own world
summary: A not-found page in the site's voice: `<title>` and `<h1>` that say it, `noindex`, one `<main>` whose first link is home, three named routes in a labelled `<nav>` and a `role="search"` GET form, every URL root-absolute because the page answers at any depth; the scene (`aria-hidden`, after the links) is the zero of 404 drawn as a sun that sets once, `translateY(-140)` over `1.8s` after `.35s` with glints opening at `.08s` steps, in CSS so it plays without script; opacity-only `.4s` under reduced motion, the last frame at once in the static tier, even when the tier flips mid-moment; README serves it with a real 404 status per host and framework
variants: drawn scene beside the copy on wide screens, a band above it on phones (this, default)
type only: the h1 at display scale reacts once (a weight or a letter shifting) with no drawing
search-led: the search field first, for a site whose routes are too many to pick three
